hypotheses.justification: `hC` follows from `hFC`. Every norm is nonnegative, so `0 ≤ ‖F 0‖ ≤ C`. In Lean: `(norm_nonneg _).trans (hFC 0)`. The proof stays the same, except that this term is passed to `mildShiftedStokesIntegral_continuousAt` instead of `hC`. `hT` can also be deleted independently of this one.

If `0 ≤ T`, use the existing proof. If `T < 0`, the function is identically zero, hence continuous. For any `t`, apply `intervalIntegral.integral_congr` on `uIcc 0 T = Icc T 0`. Every `τ` there satisfies `τ ≤ 0`, so the condition `0 < τ ∧ τ < t` in `mildShiftedStokesIntegrand` (an `if h : ...`, extended by zero) fails and the integrand is `0`. The integral is then `∫ 0 = 0`, so the map is `fun _ => 0`, which is continuous by `continuous_const`. So the theorem holds for every real `T`.
